To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the beamspace channel is sparse; 2) the number of MS antennas is typically much lower than the number of BS antennas; 3) the number of beams is typically much lower that the system dimension; 4) the beamspace precoders are able closely approximate the performance with a complexity that tracks the MSs.
the proposed B-MIMO precoding schemes can closely approximate the performance achieved by conventional MIMO precoders with complexity that scales only with the number of MS and the number of beams.

(i) beamspace MIMO communication enables near-optimal performance with reduced complexity, (ii) the performance of beamspace MIMOs with reduced-complexity linear precoders closely approaches that of their full-dimension counterparts with the same computational complexity, and (iii) the complexity of the reduced-complex precoders scales linearly with the number of MS and is independent of the system dimension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of low-complexity multi-user precoding techniques for high dimensional MIMO channels at millimeter-wave.
the development and analysis of reduced-complexity precoder designs for MU-MIMO mm-wave communication systems.
the following questions: What is the capacity of mm-wave multiuser MIMO systems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduced-complex multi-beam selection precoders are a promising approach for achieving multi-Gbit/s sum rates in MU-MIMO systems with the lowest transceivers complexity.

the proposed reduced-computational multiuser B-MIMO precoder can closely approximate the performance achieved by the full-dimensional precoder with complexity that scales linearly with the number of MS.
the proposed B-MIMO precoding schemes provide a near-optimum route for achieving multi-gigabit per second sum rates in mmWave MU-MIMO networks, with the lowest transceivers complexity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the beamspace MIMO concept is a key enabler for the realization of mm-wave MU-MIMOs.
beamspace MIMO can be used to achieve high data rates in mm-wave multi-user communication systems at a reduced complexity.
we have developed the first near-optimal multiuser precoders for mm-wave MU-MISO communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sparsity of mm-wave MIMO channels enables reduced-complexity, near-optimal multiuser precoding techniques.
the sparsity of B-MIMO channels enables a near-optimal reduction of the digital and hardware complexity in mm-wave MU systems.
B-MIMO is a promising technique for enabling the use of high-dimensional MIMO in mm-wave networks.
